headline: High-risk data leakage and cascading-error pathways exist because dexter has broad egress and file/API access while OpenBBTerminal consumes MCP/REST inputs with no documented isolation.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: dexter can write to .dexter/scratchpad/ and uses autonomous execution, while OpenBBTerminal uses MCP servers and stdin/stdout. That creates a plausible content-to-instruction bridge if OpenBBTerminal ingests dexter-produced text as trusted input. No direct shared channel is documented, so this is inferred and not higher.
conditions: IF OpenBBTerminal parses dexter output from stdin/stdout or an MCP channel as instructions
IF both agents are connected through a shared workspace or message queue
mitigations: Separate the agents onto distinct workspaces
Disable automatic parsing of free-form text between agents
Require explicit schema validation for any handoff payload
Add provenance tags to all inter-agent messages
requires-engineering: enforce channel-level allowlists

B_data_leakage.rationale: dexter touches financial and market data and has broad network egress plus multiple external APIs, while OpenBBTerminal touches financial, licensed, and public data and can use MCP/REST interfaces. If they share a workspace or principal, sensitive data can flow from one into the other and out to third parties. The exact bridge is undocumented, so uncertainty is escalated.
conditions: IF the two agents share a filesystem, API key, or OAuth principal
IF dexter forwards financial data into OpenBBTerminal MCP/REST calls
mitigations: Use separate credentials for each agent
Block shared workspaces and mount points
Redact sensitive fields before any handoff
Audit outbound destinations for both agents
requires-engineering: add per-field data-loss prevention

C_capability_conflict.rationale: dexter supports multiple instances and writes to .dexter/scratchpad/, while OpenBBTerminal does not write files or modify git state and has no shell. Overlap is limited because OpenBBTerminal is mostly read/serve oriented, so direct write-write conflict is unlikely unless an external orchestrator shares mutable state.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator maps both agents onto the same writable directory
IF OpenBBTerminal is extended with write access not shown in the profile
mitigations: Assign separate working directories
Serialize access to any shared files
Keep OpenBBTerminal read-only
Avoid shared git repositories
requires-engineering: add locking around mutable resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: dexter’s autonomous execution and external API calls can produce market or financial outputs that OpenBBTerminal may consume through MCP/REST or stdin/stdout. If OpenBBTerminal treats those outputs as authoritative without verification, errors can cascade into downstream analysis. No built-in verification step is documented, so the pathway is plausible in default integrations.
conditions: IF OpenBBTerminal consumes dexter-generated facts without independent validation
IF dexter output is routed directly into OpenBBTerminal workflows
mitigations: Require source citations on all transferred facts
Add a human review step before actioning outputs
Compare outputs against a second data source
Mark dexter outputs as untrusted by default
requires-engineering: implement verification gates

E_compliance.rationale: dexter handles financial data and broad egress, while OpenBBTerminal handles financial and licensed data. That combination can create retention, licensing, or residency mismatches if the same data class is moved between them. The profiles do not document matching compliance controls, so the safest reading is a moderate compliance risk.
conditions: IF regulated financial data is transferred from dexter into OpenBBTerminal logs or APIs
IF retention or licensing rules differ between the two deployments
mitigations: Minimize stored financial data
Review retention settings for both agents
Separate regulated and unregulated datasets
Log only metadata, not payloads
requires-engineering: align compliance controls and DPA terms
